gating: Work checkpoints 1 through 4 in order. Within each checkpoint, run unit, API, and CLI/static checks in order; do not begin the next checkpoint until its predecessor passes. All UI gates are n/a, so no UI e2e cases are planned.

unit.case: The package manifest and packed-file assertions describe the executable entry point and complete relevant tarball contents, and introduce no smol-toml runtime dependency.

Receipt retention removes only the intended stale batch, preserves young and late-arriving receipts, maintains a single concurrent claim, remains bounded in reads, and drains a backlog when writes exceed the batch size.

The CycloneDX SBOM is derived from the installed tarball's runtime graph, includes the package and runtime transitive dependencies, excludes development dependencies, and refuses missing license metadata for any included component.

Release policy refuses every publication channel when bundled-content redistribution rights are unresolved, and refuses absent, malformed, or untrusted signer fingerprints, unannotated tags, and invalid signatures before any publication side effect; an isolated 2.6.0 fixture remains unchanged.

A controlled local fixture with a valid annotated signed tag, a test-only allowlisted fingerprint, and synthetic complete rights evidence is permitted; it does not claim or configure real production authorization.

cli.case: Install the exact packed tarball in fresh npm and Bun consumers and verify the installed command's exact version output and exit status, using the installed package rather than checkout files.
Run the installed command with Bun available and Node absent, proving the Bun shebang works; when Bun is absent, verify a clear nonzero refusal without a stack trace.

Retain distinct Linux, macOS, and Windows CI results for the full serial Bun suite and existing init, doctor, uninstall, and build smoke checks; each result identifies the tested revision and includes receipt-retention coverage.

The release workflow checks out and asserts the exact dispatched SHA, completes lint, typecheck, full serial tests, and build before release build or publication, then smoke-tests, inventories, and publishes the same tarball digest without repacking.

Review README.md against actual guard behavior: it explains that the Copilot CLI adapter can fail open, command guards do not sandbox opaque programs or scripts prepared in earlier calls, and OS-level isolation is recommended for untrusted code.

blockers: Owner-verified redistribution rights for upstream bundled content, including the unresolved H4 items, remain unresolved; tests and fixtures do not establish authorization.
The owner-configured production signing fingerprint remains unresolved; do not guess, supply, or commit a real fingerprint. Keep publication blocked until an owner verifies it.
not_tested: UI e2e cases are omitted because all four checkpoint UI gates are n/a.
A synthetic permitted release fixture proves policy behavior only; it does not authorize a real signer, resolve upstream rights, publish, push, or dispatch a workflow.
